questions.question: The General Journal records:
options: Transactions that no specialised journal accommodates
All transactions of the business
Only cash transactions
Only corrections

questions.question: The fixed shape of a GJ entry is:
options: Credit line first, then debit, no explanation
Debited account first, credited account indented below, narration underneath
One line with both amounts
A column per account

questions.question: The GJ carries Debtors Control and Creditors Control analysis columns so that:
options: The trial balance can be skipped
Personal accounts need not be posted
Control-account amounts accumulate for monthly posting, like the other journals' column totals
The narration can be shorter

questions.question: Writing off L. Jacobs's irrecoverable R900 requires:
options: Debit Bad Debts R900; credit Debtors Control (and Jacobs's account) R900
Debit Debtors Control; credit Bad Debts
Debit Bank; credit Debtors Control
Debit Sales; credit Bad Debts

questions.question: Interest of R45 charged to a LATE-PAYING DEBTOR is recorded as:
options: Debit Interest Expense; credit Bank
Debit Debtors Control R45; credit Interest Income R45
Debit Interest Income; credit Debtors Control
No entry until the cash arrives

questions.question: The owner takes stock costing R350 home. The entry values the goods at:
options: Selling price, to protect profit
Half the selling price
Whatever the owner declares
Cost — no sale occurred, so no profit margin exists to record

questions.question: What all three classic entries share is that:
options: No cash moved — debts, stock or equity changed without money flowing
They all reduce profit
They all involve the bank account
They are recorded only at year end

questions.question: Stationery R250 was wrongly debited to Trading Stock. The correcting entry is:
options: Debit Stationery R250; credit Trading Stock R250
Debit Trading Stock R250; credit Stationery R250
Debit Stationery R250; credit Creditors Control R250
Debit Stationery R500; credit Trading Stock R500

questions.question: Why does the correction leave Creditors Control untouched?
options: Control accounts may never be corrected
That leg of the original entry was correct — only the broken leg is operated on
The supplier must approve first
Creditors Control fixes itself at month end

questions.question: Erasing or painting over an entry is forbidden because:
options: Ink is permanent by law
Erasing wastes time
Records must be tamper-evident — invisible alteration is where fraud lives, and visible corrections keep the books believable
The examiner prefers neat pages

subtopics.title: Control Columns and Posting the GJ

questions.question: The month's control columns show: Debtors Control dr R45, cr R900; Creditors Control cr R120. Month-end posting is:
options: Debtors Control debited R45 and credited R900; Creditors Control credited R120
One net figure of R975 to Debtors Control
Nothing — control accounts ignore the GJ
Debtors Control credited R45 and debited R900

questions.question: The GJ's month proves itself when:
options: Every narration is one sentence
The entries alternate debit and credit
The control columns are empty
Total debits across all entries equal total credits — R1 665 each in the worked month

questions.question: With the GJ in place, the six-journal system means:
options: Every transaction has exactly one front door into the books
Transactions may be recorded in any journal
The trial balance becomes optional
Cash transactions now bypass the journals

questions.question: Mrs Jacobs's vanished R900 falls to the odd-jobs book because:
options: No money moved and nothing was sold, bought or returned — every specialised diary shrugs
It is too large for the other books
Bad news always goes to the GJ
Her page is full

questions.question: The narration is described as:
options: A decoration
The one honest sentence explaining why — required because the entry is unusual
The account number
A summary of the month

questions.question: Writing a GJ entry is really:
options: A new skill unrelated to earlier work
Copying from the specialised journals
The week-one transaction analysis — two accounts, classify, direction, sides, equation — with a pen in its hand
Guesswork checked at year end

subtopics.title: Three Stories the Big Diaries Can't Tell

questions.question: The 'goodbye' story books Bad Debts because:
options: The debtor asked politely
Keeping the R900 as an asset would be the books lying to themselves — prudence demands the loss be faced
All old accounts are written off automatically
The bank requires it

questions.question: Thabo's R350 of groceries from his own shelf is drawings at cost because:
options: He drew equity in goods instead of rands, and no sale happened
Owners get a discount
The shop profits from the transfer
It counts as wages

questions.question: The interest stories teach that lateness:
options: Is only punished for customers
Is free within reason
Cancels the debt after sixty days
Has a price in both directions — the books charge it without favouritism

questions.question: The audit trail is 'worth more than perfection' because:
options: Nobody believes perfect books; everyone believes books that show their own dated, explained repairs
Perfect books attract auditors
Trails are cheaper than corrections
Errors improve the records

questions.question: The surgeon's rule for corrections is:
options: Redo the whole transaction from scratch
Operate only on the broken leg — the correct side of the original entry stays untouched
Wait for year end to fix everything at once
Erase cleanly and rewrite

questions.question: Redoing the entire stationery transaction (debit Stationery, credit Creditors again) would:
options: Fix the error twice as safely
Have no effect
Double-count the liability — creating a second error while fixing the first
Be required by the auditors
